title: Barber License Renewal Shortcut
oneLiner: A red-tape renewal checklist that turns state license paperwork changes into a 20-minute renewal packet for barbers, cosmetologists, and notaries.
targetUser: Licensed solo service workers and small shops affected by simplified 2026 renewal processes.
keyUX: Pick profession and license status, compare old steps to new steps, verify missing documents, calculate fees, and print a renewal packet before expiry.
sourceSignals: S6 - New York red-tape/license renewal simplification: https://nypost.com/2026/06/15/us-news/hochul-spells-out-50-actions-to-slash-red-tape-fees-across-new-york-and-save-1m-hours-of-time/
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app called "Barber License Renewal Shortcut" for licensed solo service workers and small shops affected by simplified 2026 renewal processes. The app is based on observed user pull: license holders already manage renewal notices, state portals, fees, training records, and changing paperwork rules, while policy changes promise simpler forms for barbers, cosmetologists, notaries, real estate professionals, and security guards. The app should use a renewal wizard mechanic around the trigger moment "a renewal reminder arrives under newly simplified rules" and make the first screen communicate "Renew before the chair goes empty." Use the user's own language: "Tell me what changed and what I still have to submit." Build the core workflow around profession, state, license expiry, fee status, continuing education, old paperwork steps, and new required steps, and produce a 20-minute renewal packet. Required sections: license countdown header, profession/state selector, old-step vs new-step diff lane, required document checklist, fee and continuing-education status, renewal portal handoff card, appointment/business interruption warning, and printable renewal packet. Emotional pressure to make visible: 자산 방어, lapsed-license fear, fee anxiety, and embarrassment in front of clients. Design direction: use the `calm-consumer` profile with warm neutral surfaces, reassuring step-by-step cards, gentle amber deadline accents, readable mobile controls, compact document states, and no decorative hero. Avoid generic dashboard framing; make the main interaction feel like a calm shortcut through red tape.
